app_documentation:
The Real-Time Inventory Management System is a modern, mobile-first application designed to help retail businesses track and manage their product inventory with real-time accuracy. Built on a React frontend with Node.js/Express backend and PostgreSQL database, the system enables store staff to scan product barcodes, monitor stock levels, receive automated low stock alerts, and generate sales reports—all through an intuitive interface optimized for both web and mobile platforms. The application leverages WebSocket technology to ensure that inventory changes are immediately reflected across all user sessions, eliminating discrepancies and enabling informed decision-making.

The system serves three primary user roles: Store Owners who need comprehensive sales analytics and business performance insights, Store Managers who oversee inventory levels and make restocking decisions, and Store Clerks who perform day-to-day operations like scanning products and updating stock quantities. Core features include barcode scanning for quick product lookup and inventory updates, real-time inventory tracking that automatically adjusts stock levels as transactions occur, customizable low stock alerts that notify users when products fall below defined thresholds, comprehensive product management capabilities for adding and editing product information, and detailed sales reporting with trend analysis and top-selling product identification.

The application's mobile-first design prioritizes quick access to critical functions through a clean, card-based interface with bottom navigation for easy one-handed operation. The barcode scanner screen provides instant camera-based product identification, while the dashboard home screen offers at-a-glance metrics including total products, low stock items, and today's sales. Real-time updates ensure that when a store clerk completes a sale or adjusts inventory, all connected users immediately see the updated stock levels without manual refresh. The system maintains a complete audit trail of all transactions, supports role-based access control, and meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards.

Designed for single-store deployments with standard UPC/EAN barcode formats, the system assumes reliable network connectivity for WebSocket synchronization and requires user authentication for all operations. The PostgreSQL database schema efficiently handles products, categories, users, transactions, and alerts with appropriate indexes for performance. Low stock alerts are generated automatically through database triggers or scheduled jobs, and the system supports customizable threshold levels per product to match specific business needs. With its combination of real-time capabilities, intuitive design, and comprehensive feature set, the Real-Time Inventory Management System provides retail businesses with the tools they need to maintain accurate inventory records and make data-driven decisions.

glossary.Barcode Scanning: The process of using a device camera or dedicated scanner to read product barcodes (UPC/EAN format) and automatically retrieve product information from the database. In this system, barcode scanning enables store staff to quickly identify products, view current stock levels, and perform inventory updates within 2 seconds of scanning a valid barcode.
glossary.Real-Time Inventory Tracking: A system capability that immediately updates and synchronizes product stock quantities across all user sessions whenever inventory changes occur through sales, restocking, or manual adjustments. Implemented using WebSocket connections, this ensures that all users see accurate, current inventory levels without needing to manually refresh their screens.
glossary.Low Stock Threshold: A configurable numeric value set for each product that defines the minimum acceptable quantity before triggering an alert notification. When a product's current stock quantity falls below its threshold (default 10 units), the system automatically generates an alert to notify store managers and owners that restocking is needed.
glossary.WebSocket: A communication protocol that enables persistent, bidirectional connections between the client application and server, allowing real-time data synchronization. In this inventory system, WebSocket connections broadcast inventory updates, alert notifications, and transaction events to all connected users instantly without requiring page refreshes or polling.
glossary.Transaction: A recorded event in the system that documents any change to product inventory, including sales, restocking, manual adjustments, and returns. Each transaction captures the product, user, transaction type, quantity changed, pricing information, timestamp, and optional notes, creating a complete audit trail for inventory management and reporting purposes.
glossary.Alert: An automated notification generated by the system when specific conditions are met, primarily when product stock levels fall below their defined low stock thresholds. Alerts are stored in the database with read/unread status, displayed on the dashboard and dedicated alerts screen, and can be configured per user role to ensure appropriate staff members are notified of inventory issues requiring attention.
